The Department of Chemical and Materials Engineering embodies Cal Poly Pomona’s polytechnic ethos, emphasizing theory, laboratory practice, and applied learning. Chemical Engineering students design sustainable processes for industries such as petrochemicals to pharmaceuticals, addressing environmental and ethical considerations. Materials Engineering students develop metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites for applications in energy, electronics, and structural systems. Faculty-led research prepares graduates for careers in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, sustainability, advanced materials, and process innovation. Students engage in real-world learning through laboratories in unit operations, process control, materials characterization, and transport phenomena, using industry-standard tools. In senior capstone projects, multidisciplinary teams tackle engineering challenges. Co-curricular organizations including AIChE, ChemE-Car, Material Advantage, ISPE, and AMPP offer community, leadership, and professional networking. Internships, along with faculty-mentored research, enrich students’ development and prepare them for engineering careers. courses.title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the professions of chemical and materials engineering. Use of computer tools, Excel and MATLAB, to solve engineering problems. Process variables and basic techniques of material balance. Corequisite(s): CHE 1411L .

courses.title: Chemical and Materials Engineering Analysis
courses.description: Data analysis and experimental design using statistical concepts and techniques applied to chemical and materials engineering systems. Analysis of plant and laboratory data. Multiple regression. Correlations and significance of correlations. Analysis of variance. Introduction to statistical process control. Corequisite(s): CHE 1421L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE major, C- or better in CHE 1311 / CHE 1411L , or C- or better in CHE 131/141L.

courses.title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Professions of Chemical and Materials (CME) engineering. Use of computer tools, Excel and MATLAB, to solve engineering problems. Process variables and basic techniques of material balance. Corequisite(s): CHE 1311 .
courses.prerequisites: MAT 105, MAT 112, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 2140 , or MAT 2240 .

courses.title: Chemical and Materials Engineering Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Data analysis and experimental design using statistical concepts and techniques applied to chemical and materials engineering systems. Analysis of plant and laboratory data. Multiple regression. Correlations and significance of correlations. Analysis of variance. Introduction to statistical process control. Corequisite(s): CHE 1321 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE major, C- or better in CHE 1311 ,/ CHE 1411L , or C- or better in CHE 131/CHE 141L.

courses.title: Introduction to Chemical and Materials Engineering Experiments Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the use of instrumentation to monitor Chemical and Materials Engineering processes. Measurement of the properties of materials. Introduction to design of experiments.
courses.prerequisites: GE Area 1A/A2; and C- or better in CHE 1311 and CHE 1411L .

courses.title: Material and Energy Balances I
courses.description: Material balances for physical and chemical processes. Use of process flow diagrams for plant mass balance calculations. Solving multi-component mass balance, simple and multiple mixing or separation problems, and chemical reaction problems including recycle and equilibrium. Energy balances for non-reactive processes.
courses.prerequisites: Chemical Engineering major; C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 122, or CHM 1210 ; and C- or better in MAT 115 or MAT 1150 .

courses.title: Material and Energy Balances II
courses.description: Analysis of single and multiple phase systems for chemical and materials engineering systems. Energy balances for both nonreactive and reactive systems. Material and energy balance analysis of transient processes. Material balance analysis of common types of reactors.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHE 201 or CHE 2011 , and C- or better in MAT 215 or MAT 2140 .

courses.title: Process and Automation
courses.description: Cross Listed as: No Dual Listed as: No Comprehensive introduction to automation and control systems, focusing on fundamental electrical circuit principles and their applications. Basic circuit laws and components, progressing into DC circuit analysis. Alternating current (AC) principles, including the behavior of capacitors, resistors, and inductors in RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Key electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, and operational amplifiers (op-amps) are introduced, emphasizing their roles in electronic systems. Exploration of sensors, sampling, data acquisition, and PID controllers, preparing students to design and implement automation systems. Concepts will be reinforced through laboratory exercises that involve building real-world applications using the Arduino platform. Corequisite(s): CHE 2301L .
courses.prerequisites: MAT 215 or MAT 2140 ; CHE 201, CHE 2011 , IME 113L, or IME 1130L ; and C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Process and Automation Laboratory
courses.description: Comprehensive introduction to automation and control systems, focusing on fundamental electrical circuit principles and their applications. Basic circuit laws and components, progressing into DC circuit analysis. Alternating current (AC) principles, including the behavior of capacitors, resistors, and inductors in RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Key electronic devices such as diodes, transistors, and operational amplifiers (op-amps) are introduced, emphasizing their roles in electronic systems. Exploration of sensors, sampling, data acquisition, and PID controllers, preparing students to design and implement automation systems. Concepts will be reinforced through laboratory exercises that involve building real-world applications using the Arduino platform. Corequisite(s): CHE 2301
courses.prerequisites: MAT 215 or MAT 2140 ; CHE 201, CHE 2011 , IME 113L, or IME 1130L ; and C- or better in PHY 133 or PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Applied Mathematics in Chemical and Materials Engineering
courses.description: A study in the application of basic linear algebra, derivative, and integral concepts to solve chemical and materials engineering problems. Use of first-order ordinary differential equations to solve transient materials and energy balances. Use of MATLAB to solve set of non-linear algebraic equations and set of ordinary differential equations. Corequisite(s): MAT 2240 .
courses.prerequisites: Chemical Engineering major; MAT 215, MAT 216, or MAT 2140 ; and C- or better in CHE 201 or CHE 2011 .

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics I
courses.description: Energy and its transformations; conversion of heat to work; first and second law analyses; property relationships; equations of state; equilibrium at minimum Gibbs free energy, Clausius-Clapeyron equation, vapor-liquid phase equilibria for pure fluids and mixtures of ideal solutions; thermodynamics of mixtures; partial molar properties and excess Gibbs free energy.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 2070 or MTE 207; MAT 2240 , MAT 224, or MAT 216; PHY 1520 or PHY 133; C- or better in CHE 2021 or CHE 202; and CHE major or MTE minor.

courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics II
courses.description: Solution thermodynamics. Vapor-liquid phase equilibria of ideal and non-ideal solutions. Definition and applications of fugacity, activity, and activity coefficient. Equation of state calculation of mixture properties. Activity coefficient models: van Laar, Wilson, and NRTL models. Gibbs free energy changes of mixing and phase changes. Distillation and multi-component flash process calculations.
courses.prerequisites: CHE 302 or CHE 3021 .

courses.title: Kinetics & Reactor Design
courses.description: Chemical reaction equilibria. Equilibrium constant and the standard Gibbs free energy of reaction. Product distributions in single and multiple reactions. Mole balances. Levenspiel plots. Homogeneous and heterogeneous reaction kinetics for both chemical and materials engineering systems. Analysis of kinetic data. Reactor design, including batch, continuous-stirred tank flow, packed-bed, and plug flow reactors. Isothermal and non-isothermal reactor design.
courses.prerequisites: CHE 302 or CHE 3021 ; and CHM 201, CHM 314, CHM 2010 , or CHM 3140 .

courses.title: Transport Phenomena I
courses.description: Introduction to fluid mechanics and heat transfer with application to the unit operations of chemical engineering. Topics include dimensional analysis, fluid properties, kinematics and dynamics of fluid flow, friction, boundary conditions, piping calculations, energy transfer by conduction, convection and radiation, and heat exchanger design. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): CHE 3221LW .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 2851 , PHY 1520 , MTE 2070 , C- or better in CHE 2021 , CHE major or MTE minor, and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Transport Phenomena II
courses.description: Heat and mass transport with applications to the unit operations of chemical engineering. Topics include steady and transient heat transfer, convective heat transfer, radiation heat transfer, heat exchanger design, steady and transient mass transfer, convective mass transfer, distillation, absorption, stripping, and water treatment.Mass transport with applications to the unit operations of chemical engineering and environmental problems, including topics in distillation, absorption, stripping, flue gas desulfurization, and water chemical, physicochemical, and biological treatment. Corequisite(s): CHE 3331L .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 311 or CHE 3111W .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry for Chemical Engineers
courses.description: Chemical reactions of organic compounds in relation to the chemical and materials industries.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 .

courses.title: Transport Laboratory II
courses.description: Applying experimental design and the basic concepts in transport phenomena in experimental study of both chemical and materials engineering systems that may involve diffusivity measurement, batch distillation, heat exchanger, membrane separation, droplet evaporation, heat transfer in extended surfaces and others. Corequisite(s): CHE 3121 .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 311 or CHE 3111W , and CHE 322L or CHE 3221LW .

courses.title: Unit Operations and Pollution Abatement
courses.description: Treatment of mass, momentum and heat transport viewed with the traditional unit operations emphasis. Multi-component and multiphase systems are considered, with some problems involving design. Topics include distillation, cooling tower, absorption and heat exchanger design.
courses.prerequisites: CHE 312 or CHE 3121 ; CHE 304 or CHE 3040; CHE 303 or CHE 3031; and CHE 333L or CHE 3331L.

courses.title: Process Controls
courses.description: Introduction to theory, design, and application of automatic control systems to chemical and physical processes. Topics include transfer function, control valve sizing, PID controller tuning, multivariable process control, and MATLAB Simulink. 2 hours lectures/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: CHE 2301 , and CHE 333L or CHE 3331L .

courses.title: Chemical Safety and Hazardous Materials Management
courses.description: Improve the understanding of natural processes and the fundamentals that govern the concentrations of contaminants in water, air, and other media. Topics in air pollution, water pollution, and solid waste.
courses.prerequisites: MAT 116, MAT 224, or MAT 2240 ; CHM 201, CHM 314, or CHM 3140 ; CHE 302 or CHE 3021 ; and CHE 311 or CHE 3111W .

courses.title: Unit Operation and Process Control Laboratory
courses.description: Treatment of mass, momentum and heat transport viewed with the traditional unit operations emphasis. Multi-component and multiphase systems are considered, with some problems involving design. Distillation, absorption and heat exchanger design. Experimental study of the dynamics and control of chemical engineering processes using single-loop, PID controllers. Simulation of real control systems. Hardware requirements for real control systems. Corequisite(s): CHE 426 or CHE4260.
courses.prerequisites: ECE 231 or CHE 2301 ; CHE 333L or CHE 3331L ; and CHE 4251 .

courses.title: Chemical Process Synthesis and Design I
courses.description: Design of major equipment common to most chemical industries. Emphasis on how equipment fits together and interacts in an integrated process. Design of steam and refrigeration cycles. Treatment of process design methodology. Process flow diagrams and piping and instrumentation diagrams. Energy integration in plant design. Optimization strategies in process design. Introduction to ammonia synthesis and oil refining. Use of process simulators. Corequisite(s): CHE 4450L .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 304 or CHE 3040 ; CHE 312 or CHE 3121; CHE 333L or CHE 3331L; and CHE 303 or CHE 3031.

courses.title: Chemical Process Synthesis and Design I Laboratory
courses.description: Design of major equipment common to most chemical industries. Emphasis on how equipment fits together and interacts in an integrated process. Design of steam and refrigeration cycles. Treatment of process design methodology. Process flow diagrams and piping and instrumentation diagrams. Energy integration in plant design. Optimization strategies in process design. Introduction to ammonia synthesis and oil refining. Use of process simulators. Corequisite(s): CHE 4450 .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 304 or CHE 3040 , CHE 312 or CHE 3121 , CHE 333L or CHE 3331L , and CHE 303 or CHE 3031 .

courses.title: Chemical Process Synthesis and Design II
courses.description: Team project to perform process design and economic analysis of a complete plant with attention to environmental constraints including state and federal laws. Discussions on contemporary issues. Emphasis on team effort, effective communication, plant design procedure, plant management and control. Use of process simulators. Corequisite(s): CHE 4451L .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 441 or CHE 4450 , and CHE 451L or CHE 4450L .

courses.title: Chemical Process Synthesis and Design II Laboratory
courses.description: Team project to perform process design and economic analysis of a complete plant with attention to environmental constraints including state and federal laws. Discussions on contemporary issues. Emphasis on team effort, effective communication, plant design procedure, plant management and control. Use of process simulators. Corequisite(s): CHE 4451 .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 441 or CHE 4450 , and CHE 451L or CHE 4450L .

courses.title: Undergraduate Research Project
courses.description: Final state of major project work. Emphasis on effective communication and critical thinking of research project results.
courses.prerequisites: EGR 482 or EGR 4810 .

courses.title: Professional Development and Case Studies in Chemical and Materials Engineering Activity
courses.description: Case studies on the fundamental concepts of mathematics, stoichiometry, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, kinetics and reactor design, unit operations, process controls, materials, and corrosion. Topics for discussion included oral and written communications skills, environmental, legal, energy, and ethics issues.
courses.prerequisites: CHE 441 or CHE 4450 , and CHE 451L or CHE 4450L .

courses.title: Materials Science and Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals and applications of materials engineering. Atomic, molecular, and crystalline structures and properties of materials with their relevance to engineering. Topics will include: diffusion, defects, phase diagrams, heat treatment, mechanical behavior, and will cover the different materials classes, i.e., metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1210 , CHM 1150 , CHM 121, or CHM 115; PHY 131 or PHY 1510 ; PHY 131L or PHY 1510L ; and MAT 116 or MAT 1150 .

courses.title: Polymer Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the structure, properties, behavior, and processing of polymers as engineering materials. Design of reinforced and unreinforced polymers, and the processing methods used in the manufacture of products. Corequisite(s): MTE 3030L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and ME 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, or MTE 3170L ; and CHE 311, CHE 3111W , ME 311, ME 3111 , ARO 301, or ARO 3011 .

courses.title: Polymer Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the structure, properties, behavior, and processing of polymers as engineering materials. Design of reinforced and unreinforced polymers, and the processing methods used in the manufacture of products. Corequisite(s): MTE 3030 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and ME 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, or MTE 3170L ; and CHE 311, CHE 3111W , ME 311, ME 3111 , ARO 301, or ARO 3011 .

courses.title: Materials Science and Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experiences to reinforce fundamental materials engineering concepts. Crystal models, microscopy, hardness tests, strengthening, and heat treatment. Materials selection and design. Emphasis on technical written and oral communication skills. Safety awareness reinforced throughout the course. Elements of statistics and experimental design.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207 or MTE 2070 .

courses.title: Mechanical Metallurgy
courses.description: A comprehensive exploration of the field of mechanical metallurgy including the continuum description of stress and strain, the flow and fracture of metals from the defect mechanism point of view, the tests used for determining mechanical properties, and the fundamental/analytical techniques applied to the various metalworking processes used in industry. Corequisite(s): MTE 3200L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, or MTE 3170L .

courses.title: Mechanical Metallurgy Laboratory
courses.description: A comprehensive exploration of the field of mechanical metallurgy including the continuum description of stress and strain, the flow and fracture of metals from the defect mechanism point of view, the tests used for determining mechanical properties, and the fundamental/analytical techniques applied to the various metalworking processes used in industry. Corequisite(s): MTE 3200 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and ME 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, MTE 3170L .

courses.title: Functional Materials
courses.description: Advanced concepts of materials science and their relevance to engineering. Origin of electronic, thermal, magnetic and optical properties. Applications of electronic, magnetic, and optical materials. Corequisite(s): MTE 3270L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; ME 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, or MTE 3170L ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Functional Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Advanced concepts of materials science and their relevance to engineering. Origin of electronic, thermal, magnetic and optical properties. Applications of electronic, magnetic, and optical materials. Corequisite(s): MTE 3270 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; ME 350L, ME 3501L , MTE 317L, or MTE 3170L ; PHY 133 or PHY 1520 ; and PHY 133L or PHY 1520L .

courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: Macroscopic thermodynamics, the study of energy and its transformations, as it applies to the field of materials in the solid and liquid state. Detailed topics to be covered are the first and second law, property relationships, equilibrium, electrochemistry, solutions and mixing, phase rule and phase diagrams. In addition, an introduction to microscopic thermodynamics or statistical thermodynamics will be included as it applies to the understanding of the macroscopic properties and behavior of materials.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 .

courses.title: Joining of Materials
courses.description: Introduction to the principles, methods and applications of joining as they apply to the metals, ceramics, plastics, and electronic industries. Included are fasteners, welding, brazing, soldering, adhesives, diffusion and ultrasonic bonding. Principles of mechanical, chemical, and physical phenomena related to surfaces and the mechanics of joints. The approach will be to unify the principles underlying diverse engineering technologies to the basic science of the joining processes.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Joining of Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the principles, methods and applications of joining as they apply to the metals, ceramics, plastics, and electronic industries. Included are fasteners, welding, brazing, soldering, adhesives, diffusion and ultrasonic bonding. Principles of mechanical, chemical, and physical phenomena related to surfaces and the mechanics of joints. The approach will be to unify the principles underlying diverse engineering technologies to the basic science of the joining processes.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Kinetic Processes in Materials
courses.description: Physical chemistry applied to materials engineering. Topics include: surfaces and interfaces; nucleation and growth theory; diffusional and non-diffusional transformations; precipitation from the solid solution, reaction kinetics, transport, and introduction to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Computational Materials Engineering
courses.description: Fundamentals of computational materials sciences, such as molecular dynamics, first-principles calculation, density functional theory, and phase-field simulation. Students will gain familiarity with stateoftheart methods to model and simulate materials and handson experience using these methods. A broad range of modeling techniques will be covered that span from atomistic to continuum domains. Applications will be presented that utilize computational tools to study the structural, mechanical, chemical, and electronic properties of materials.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , or ME 3150 ; MTE 317L or MTE 3170L .

courses.title: Corrosion And Materials Degradation
courses.description: Fundamental principles of corrosion science, application of these principles to corrosion engineering problems and materials selection. Topics to be covered include: thermodynamics and kinetics of metallic corrosion; corrosive/destructive environments, the different forms of corrosion and degradation, corrosion/degradation prevention; principles of materials selection. Corequisite(s): MTE 4010L .
courses.prerequisites: ME 302, ME 3121 , CHE 303, or CHE 3031 ; MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Corrosion And Materials Degradation Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamental principles of corrosion science, application of these principles to corrosion engineering problems and materials selection. Topics to be covered include: thermodynamics and kinetics of metallic corrosion; corrosive/destructive environments, the different forms of corrosion and degradation, corrosion/degradation prevention; principles of materials selection. Corequisite(s): MTE 4010 .
courses.prerequisites: CHE 3031 , ME 3121 , CHE 303, or ME 302; MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Electronic Materials
courses.description: Advanced concepts of electronic materials and their engineering applications. Physical principles, processing, and materials selection for circuits, magnets, transducers, memories, integrated circuits, displays and superconductors.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Physical Metallurgy - Mechanical Properties
courses.description: Basic principles underlying the structure and properties of crystalline solids. Metallic and covalent bonding theories; crystallography; solid solutions; intermetallic compounds and alloys. Crystal imperfections; elastic and plastic deformation. Ductile and brittle fracture, fatigue and creep.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and ME 301, ME 3011 , CHE 302, CHE 3021 , or MTE 3280 .

courses.title: Physical Metallurgy - Solidification and Strengthening Reactions
courses.description: Principles of solid-state reactions including elementary kinetics, nucleation and growth theory; annealing of cold-worked metals; diffusionless transformation, precipitation reactions and tempering; physical metallurgy of steels; relation between properties and microstructure. Laboratory experiments related to phase transformations in steel, solidification structures, precipitation hardening, and plant trips. Corequisite(s): MTE 4060L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L ; ME 301 or ME 3011 ; and CHE 302, CHE 3021 , or MTE 3280 .

courses.title: Physical Metallurgy Solidification and Strengthening Reactions Laboratory
courses.description: Principles of solid-state reactions including elementary kinetics, nucleation and growth theory; annealing of cold-worked metals; diffusionless transformation, precipitation reactions and tempering; physical metallurgy of steels; relation between properties and microstructure. Laboratory experiments related to phase transformations in steel, solidification structures, precipitation hardening, and plant trips. Corequisite(s): MTE 4060 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L ; ME 301 or ME 3011 ; and CHE 302, CHE 3021 , or MTE 3280 .

courses.title: Ceramic Materials
courses.description: The composition, structure, and properties of ceramic bodies employed as structural and non-structural materials, with an emphasis on processing and their physical state, elasticity, strength, and optical, thermal, and electrical properties. Laboratory experiments related to fabrication, testing, statistical analysis, and plant trips Corequisite(s): MTE 4070L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Ceramic Materials Laboratory
courses.description: The composition, structure, and properties of ceramic bodies employed as structural and non-structural materials, with an emphasis on processing and their physical state, elasticity, strength, and optical, thermal, and electrical properties. Laboratory experiments related to fabrication, testing, statistical analysis, and plant trips. Corequisite(s): MTE 4070 .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Composite Materials
courses.description: Introduction to composite materials engineering processing and mechanics. Properties and processing of fibers and matrices. Polymer matrix composites, metal matrix composites, ceramic composites and carbon/carbon. Lamina and laminate constitutive equations. Laminate strength analysis. Corequisite(s): MTE 4080L .
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.description: Integration of the undergraduate courses in the basic sciences, engineering sciences, materials engineering, economics, business, and general education in the integrated solution of materials selection and design problems. Analysis, selection, and evaluation of materials and processes aimed at product development. Use of numeric based selection criteria will be emphasized culminating in professional reports and presentations.

courses.description: Complete overview of materials characterization and testing for metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. Macroscopic characterization of the mechanical, electrical, and optical properties. Microscopic evaluation using x-ray, diffraction, SEM, EDAX, TEM, IR-spectroscopy, and ultrasound evaluation techniques.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Fracture and Failure Analysis
courses.description: Basic principles of fracture mechanics, and applications to failure analysis. Topics include: elements of fracture mechanics, ductile and brittle fracture, residual stresses, creep, fatigue, environmental effects, statistical distributions, and design issues. The approach will emphasize case histories (including guest lectures from practicing engineers on actual studies) and student presentations.
courses.prerequisites: MTE 207, MTE 2070 , ME 315, or ME 3150 ; and MTE 317L, MTE 3170L , ME 350L, or ME 3501L .

courses.title: Materials Thermodynamics
courses.description: Advanced macroscopic thermodynamics applied to materials in the solid and liquid states. Laws of thermodynamics, important thermodynamic functions, multicomponent phase equilibria, electrochemistry, solutions and mixing, phase rule and phase diagrams. Discussion of applications and statistical thermodynamics.

courses.title: Mechanical Properties of Materials
courses.description: Study of the mechanical behavior of materials. Fundamental mechanisms controlling deformation and fracture in solid materials. Strain hardening, creep, fatigue, ductile and brittle fracture. Strengthening mechanisms involving alloying and heat treatment. Superplasticity. 3 hours lecture/problem solving.

courses.title: Phase Transformations
courses.description: Principles of solid-state reactions including nucleation and growth theory, diffusional and shear transformations, the shape-memory effect, transformation toughening, thermal treatment of solids. Special topics include metallic and silicate glasses, physical metallurgy of steels and superalloys.

courses.title: Advanced Corrosion and Environmental Degradation
courses.description: Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion. Nernst and Tafel equations. Pourbaix diagrams. Electrochemical basis for corrosion. Fundamental approach to corrosion and corrosion control. Microbially Induced Corrosion. Biofouling. Degradation of polymers. Weathering of structural and architectural materials.

courses.title: Materials Processing
courses.description: Mass, heat and momentum transfer applied to materials processing. Topics: fluid properties, dynamic flow, conductive, convective and radiative heat transfer. Mass transport and solid state diffusion. Materials processing operations, e.g., solidification / casting, carburization, chemical vapor deposition, doping, etc.
courses.prerequisites: Undergraduate course in materials science, transport phenomena.

courses.title: Materials for Energy Applications
courses.description: Materials science relevant to energy generation and storage. Thermodynamics, electrochemistry, catalysis, and polymer materials science to understand polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells. Role of materials in solid oxide fuel cells, batteries, wind, solar, ocean thermal, and nuclear energy generation. Electronic band structure and photovoltaics. Artificial leaves.

courses.title: Composite Materials
courses.description: Materials science and engineering of composite materials. Special emphasis will be on the structure-property relationships. Classification of Composites. Macromolecular Science. Processing and Production of Composite Materials. Constituent materials and Characterization. Macro- & micro-mechanics. Manufacturing and Machining Methods. Testing and Inspection. Fabrication, defect detection, analysis and repair. Sandwich Panels. Life cycle. Adhesive bonding and mechanical/bonded joints. Applications.

courses.title: Nanomaterials
courses.description: Fundamental understanding of nanomaterials science. Limits to strengthening of materials at the nanoscale. Thermodynamics and kinetics at the nanoscale. Effects of dimensionality and scale. Graphene, nanotubes, fullerenes, and nanocomposites.

courses.title: Biomaterials
courses.description: Materials and their interactions with biological hosts. Biological strategies for materials synthesis. Bio-inspired materials. Hierarchical and cellular structure of biomaterials, e.g., bones and muscles. Bio-composites. Damage, degradation, and restoration of biomaterials.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project
courses.description: A continuation of work on a Master’s Degree Project after a student has completed the required MTE 6910. Presentations of projects in acceptable written and oral form to a committee of faculty in the Department required. The project proposal, plan, and schedule need to be approved by the advisor. Regular meetings and discussions with the faculty advisor should continue until the completion of the project. Credit will be assigned upon acceptance of the project by the defense committee.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, advancement to Candidacy, completion of all relevant coursework, and an approved project topic by the faculty advisor.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Independent investigation intended to be an extension of an existing body of knowledge into an area not thoroughly investigated before, directed by a committee of graduate faculty members, and resulting in a published thesis. Must be repeated as appropriate. Credit assigned upon successful completion of entire thesis and approval of the committee.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 6 units.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Comprehensive examination to satisfy the culminating experience requirement of the Master of Science in Materials Engineering (MSMT) degree. May enroll after completing the required course work, and it may be taken up to two times.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, consent of instructor, and good standing.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
